claims.text: An integrated multiscale simulation framework will accurately describe heat transport in HfNbTaTiZr.
Separately predicting lattice and electronic thermal conductivity avoids conflating the two heat-transport channels.
Accounting for mass disorder and oxygen-induced local lattice distortions will improve the description of heat transport in HfNbTaTiZr.
The lattice and electronic thermal-conductivity contributions in HfNbTaTiZr will be nearly equal below 200 K.
The total thermal conductivity of HfNbTaTiZr containing 1 wt.% oxygen will remain within 10–17 W/(K·m) from 300 K to 1200 K.
The proposed framework will improve predictive accuracy by at least 20% relative to conventional Debye or perfect-crystal models.
Adding 1 wt.% oxygen to HfNbTaTiZr introduces defect-induced scattering.
Adding 1 wt.% oxygen to HfNbTaTiZr introduces mass disorder.
Mass disorder and oxygen-related point defects produce local lattice distortions.
Local lattice distortions modify the vibrational spectrum.
Local lattice distortions modify electron-scattering rates.
Temperature-dependent anharmonic phonon spectra and electronic band structures can be used to decouple lattice and electronic thermal-conductivity contributions.
Separately computed electron and phonon scattering matrices can apportion total thermal conductivity into lattice and electronic channels.
Calibration with experimental electron–phonon scattering data will improve the scattering treatment in the disordered alloy.
Existing analytical approaches rely on perfect-crystal approximations or simplified Debye models.
Existing analytical approaches fail to capture atomic-scale disorder and independently resolved transport channels in high-entropy alloys.
The proposed framework is applicable from 30 K to 1200 K.
Uncertainty in electron–phonon coupling for highly disordered systems may limit the framework's accuracy.
The precision of experimental calibration may limit the framework's accuracy.
